role: Sharpen engine juror (senior X ghostwriter and copy chief)
verdict: v4.2's Claude path now matches Typefully's AI rewrite on edit quality and beats it on safety and restraint. On the fourth blind set it scored 98.3% postable (98.6% on lines that need work) with 0 misses, 0 broken sentences and 0 facts or meanings changed; it left 47/48 sharp lines and every deadpan frame alone, kept hard-news framing, and gave a true receipt on every line Claude itself wrote. With the strict instant line and strict fallbacks the app no longer surfaces a broken engine line. The on-device engine clears its P0: 90.8% / 91.7% postable and 0 broken lines on set 4, and every broken line from sets 1-3 now comes out whole; what's left is policy (it cuts deadpan frames such as 'Breaking:' on sharp jokes) and a few receipt slips.
to_95_ondevice: Deadpan frames: never cut a label ('Breaking:', 'Fun fact:', 'Update:', 'Life update:') when the rest of the line has no other marks and is a complete short sentence. Match the prompt, which keeps them (y-7, y-38, y-67, y-101).

Frame coverage: treat 'if I'm being real/transparent' like 'If I'm honest' (y-20, y-58). Trim list headers 'Here are a few of …, in case you're looking for …' and 'Here's a list of N … that' the way Claude does (y-51, y-66). On a >280 line, cut an 'I've been sitting on this … which is that' run-up (y-42).

Receipts: fire the hard-news receipt only on hard-news words used about the writer or someone close (not 'the market spent the week dying', y-106). Never call a deadpan label a 'run-up'. In the rules fallback, never say 'The run-up is gone' when the line still opens on one (y-42).
Homepage put-back: keep the question mark when a put-back word reopens a question (y-23: 'ok but why does … after a week.').

issues.where: core.js label cuts (kind 'label') on already-sharp lines
issues.problem: The engine cuts deadpan frames from 4 of the 11 sharp lines that carry one: y-7 'Fun fact:', y-38 'Breaking:', y-67 'Life update:', y-101 'Update:'. It keeps 'Plot twist:', 'TIL:', 'Breaking news:', 'Reminder:' and 'Honest question:'. y-38 loses the joke: 'Founder discovers that customers want the thing they asked for.' reads flat, and the receipt calls the frame a run-up. Claude keeps all four, and in the app the 'already sharp' restore puts the writer's line back, so this bites on the homepage demo.
issues.fix: Make label cuts conditional: if the body after the label is one or two complete sentences with no other soft marks, keep the label and return 'clean' with 'Your frame sets up the joke.' Add Fun fact, Breaking, Update, Life update and PSA to the deadpan list the prompt already keeps.

issues.problem: A few frames and headers survive while their siblings are cut: 'if i'm being real,' (y-20) and 'If I'm being transparent,' (y-58), but 'If I'm honest' is cut in y-31 and y-96. List headers 'Here are a few of the newsletters …, in case you're looking for something new to read:' (y-51) and 'Here's a list of 7 questions that' (y-66) are untouched. Long run-ups 'I've been sitting on this … which is that' (y-42) and the set-1 lines u-34 and u-69 stay.
issues.fix: Group 'if I'm (being) honest/real/transparent/frank' in one pattern. Trim 'Here are a few of the X' -> 'A few X' with ', in case you're looking for …' as a tail cut, and 'Here's a list of N X that' -> 'N X'. On a >280 line, cut a 'sitting on this … decided it's time to share … which is that' run-up as one throat span.

issues.where: hard-news detector; label why; rules why
issues.problem: y-106, a joke ('The NFT market spent the week dying.'), gets 'Kept as written. On news like this, your framing is how you chose to tell it.' y-7 and y-38 call a deadpan label 'the run-up'. y-19 says 'Marked “update”, not cut: without it this line breaks or says something else. Your call.', which confuses more than it helps. The y-42 rules fallback says 'The run-up is gone' while the line still opens on 'I've been sitting on this…'.
issues.fix: Fire hard news only on loss words about a person, pet, job, home or health (died, passed away, diagnosed, laid off, let go, lost our …), not about markets. Word the label receipt as 'Your frame'. Make the run-up receipt check that no throat/announce span remains in the line's first clause.

issues.where: concepts/r86/home.html toggleWord with the engine's keep option
issues.problem: y-23: Sharpen gives 'why does every productivity app turn into a second job after a week?'. Putting 'ok but' back gives '…after a week.' The question mark the engine added is lost.
issues.fix: In sharpenLine's end-punctuation tidy, add '?' when the first clause after any kept opener starts with a wh-word or an auxiliary, not only when the line starts with one.

issues.problem: Claude cuts 'ngl' from an already-sharp casual line (y-28) and keeps 'Here's my honest take on X:' as a frame (y-2, y-45, y-57, y-71, y-99), while the engine cuts that run-up. Both are defensible, but the demo and the app now differ on the 'honest take' class, and y-99 trims only 'honest', which is a half-step.
issues.fix: Pick one rule and state it in both places. I'd treat 'Here's my honest take on X:' as a run-up that may go when X is the subject of the claim after the colon, and keep it when the line ends at the colon (a thread header, as in y-36 and y-85). Add 'ngl' at the start of a short sharp line to the voice-keep list.

issues.problem: These Claude lines came from a stand-in at default effort, while production runs Opus 5.5 at low effort with a 12 s timeout. Set 4 was also weighted toward break traps where the right edit is light or none, so h% runs higher than on sets 1-3. Set 3 (95.8% Claude, 0 errors) is the fairer baseline.
issues.fix: Re-run sets 1-4 through sharpenClaude at production settings. Report postable %, timeouts, cap and rules fallbacks per set, and quote the 480-line pooled number.
